notes: The access curriculum behind the platform's 20 learner-type modules: how teachers, parents, stewards and assessors read learning states (flow, stretch, overload, shutdown, recovery) and design access so every learner reaches the same real transfer checks. Grounded in universal-design practice: the capability is the constant, the format is the variable; profiles are supports chosen by the learner and family, never diagnoses or labels; nothing here is medical advice, and families are always pointed to their school's own evaluation and support processes for formal services. Transfer checks are performed on the adult's own classroom, home or hall — real rooms, real learners (with consent), real materials.

themes.description: The band between boredom and overwhelm where learning compounds — what flow looks like in a real learner, at any age, in any subject.
themes.transfer_check: Observe one learner (with consent) for ten minutes and note two visible signs that placed them in, above, or below the flow channel.

bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to recognise and design for the real flow channel.

bands.K–2: Sit somewhere comfortable to do your work, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find a real comfortable place to focus, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify how a real neutral space can equalise real access, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use a real neutral space deliberately to support your own real access.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else why a real shared space can equalise access.

themes.description: Spoons and flares — planning sessions with variable-capacity learners around their honest energy, not the timetable's.
themes.transfer_check: Co-plan one week with a variable-energy learner using their own energy forecast, and compare plan to reality without blame.

bands.K–2: Notice when you're getting tired, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Track your own real energy through the day, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Account for real energy levels when planning real tasks, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan your own real day around your real energy levels, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to do real energy accounting for their own day.

themes.description: Recorded benches, catch-up paths and split checks — so illness interrupts progress without erasing it.
themes.transfer_check: Make one real unit absence-proof (record it, chunk it, split its check) and walk a returning learner through the catch-up.

bands.K–2: Catch up on what you missed with an adult's help.
bands.3–5: Learn how to catch up after missing a real day, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Design a real way to make learning resilient to real absence, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build a real absence-proof plan for your own real learning, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to design real learning that survives real absence.

themes.description: The agreed signal, the reset space, and the shame-free way back in — designed before it's needed.
themes.transfer_check: Agree an exit-and-return protocol with one learner and rehearse it once calmly before any real use.

bands.K–2: Know a safe place to go if you need a break, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn a real way to step out and come back to a real task, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Use a real exit and return plan appropriately, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use your own real exit-and-return strategy during real work, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to design a real exit-and-return system.

themes.description: The learner who cannot perform the motion directing another's hands step by step — full mastery, different muscles.
themes.transfer_check: Have one learner pass a real hands-on check entirely by directing a partner's hands, and score the direction's precision.

bands.K–2: Use your hands to help you think, like drawing, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Use a real hands-on activity to help understand something, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Use real hands-on activity to support real understanding, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Use your own real hands-on strategies to support real learning, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to direct the hands to support real thinking.

themes.theme: The whole team around the learner
themes.description: Family, school supports, and where they exist the learner's own care plans — the platform as one voice in a chorus, never a replacement for it.
themes.transfer_check: Map the real support team around one learner (with the family) and mark what this platform carries and what belongs to others.

bands.K–2: Get help from family and teachers together, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Work with a real team of adults supporting a real learner, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Coordinate a real team of supports around a real learner, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Coordinate your own real support team around your real needs, on your own.
bands.11–12: Lead a real coordinated team effort around a real learner's needs.
